title: Kojima et al. 2024 (Dataset B) — Four-class ASME BCI: investigation of the feasibility and comparison of two strategies for multiclassing
description: This dataset comprises EEG recordings from 15 healthy subjects performing an auditory brain-computer interface task based on the ASME (Auditory Stream segregation Multiclass ERP) paradigm. The study investigates two strategies for achieving four-class classification: ASME-4stream (four independent streams with single target stimuli) and ASME-2stream (two streams with dual target stimuli each). EEG data were recorded at 1000 Hz from 64 channels during 12 runs per subject, with offline analysis including event-related potential characterization, binary classification, and BCI simulation using linear discriminant analysis.
methods_description: EEG was recorded at 1000 Hz from 64 channels (64 EEG + 2 EOG) using a BrainAmp system with EasyCap electrodes referenced to the right mastoid. Subjects performed 12 runs alternating between ASME-4stream (4 streams, SOA=150ms, 600 stimuli/trial) and ASME-2stream (2 streams, SOA=300ms, 300 stimuli/trial) paradigms. Preprocessing included ICA-based artifact removal (15 components), bandpass filtering (1-40 Hz for ERP analysis, 0.1-8 Hz for classification), epoching (-0.1 to 1.2s), and downsampling to 250 Hz. Classification employed shrinkage-LDA with mean amplitudes from 10 non-overlapping intervals (0-1.0s) as features, evaluated via 4-fold chronological cross-validation.
